end.summary:
- Discussed water as liquid, ice, and invisible water vapour.
- Practised evaporation using drying clothes; Sana explained that water goes into the air as invisible water.
- Practised the role of heat or warmth in drying.
- Sana still described water as having only one form at the end; this mix-up was not corrected after the last mention.
- Discussed that water can move into the air rather than disappearing.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the three forms of water and changes such as evaporation, using drying clothes as an example. Sana connected warmth with faster drying and later said that water goes into the air as invisible water. They still mixed up the idea that water has three forms at the end of the lesson. At home, ask Sana to find one example each of liquid water, ice, and water vapour, then explain where the water goes when wet clothes dry.
